title: How long is the blue line on this number line?
description: A blue line runs from zero to the first mark on a number line where the distance from zero to one is cut into two equal parts. The board finds the size of one part, counts the parts under the blue line and checks that two parts fill one unit. Keeko doubts the answer by reading the first mark as the number one.
teaching_notes: One idea: cut one unit into equal parts, then count the parts a line covers to read its length. Watch for students who read the first mark as one instead of counting parts.

source: On a number line from 0 to 2, the distance from 0 to 1 is di
video_script.why: A learner reads a length on the number line by cutting the unit into equal parts and counting the parts.
video_script.substitution: the book's own number line from 0 to 2 with the unit cut into two equal parts
video_script.anchor: the number line from 0 to 2 with a blue line from 0 to the first mark
video_script.wrong_answer: the blue line is one unit long
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads the first mark as the number one, so the blue line is called one unit long, although the mark labelled one is further along.
video_script.payoff_line: The blue line is one half of a unit long

final_answer.spoken: the blue line is one half of a unit long

never_show: 1 unit as the length of the blue line
maths_rules: the distance from 0 to 1 is 1 unit
1 unit cut into 2 equal parts: each part is 1/2 unit
the blue line covers 1 part, so it is 1 x 1/2 = 1/2 unit long
check: 2 x 1/2 = 1 unit, the distance from 0 to 1
video_script.design: One number line from 0 to 2 stays all video. The unit is cut in two, the blue line covers one part, and Keeko's doubt reads the first mark as one.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the blue line is one unit long, because it ends at the first mark.
<bookmark mark='label'/>But look where the label one sits. It is further along, past the blue line.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The blue line stops before it, so it is shorter than one unit.
We count equal parts, not marks, and the blue line covers one of the two.
